### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **2** package(s): `@objectstack/formula`, `@objectstack/spec`, touching **12** documentable anchor(s).

**2** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/automation/flows.mdx`  _(via validateExpression (symbol, a top-level function))_
- `content/docs/data-modeling/formulas.mdx`  _(via validateExpression (symbol, a top-level function))_

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **3** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **60** of **216** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **156** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **156**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **101** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **169** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 0be247ce8b91ba3b9a3ce7235491b28a986b039a` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `91d2d53f86c7b64a4f9aefd6183e1a5de4ea2970` — the merge of head `e029ea772b1555ea33b2946e0978ff4175dbdd3e` into base `0be247ce8b91ba3b9a3ce7235491b28a986b039a`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 91d2d53f86c7b64a4f9aefd6183e1a5de4ea2970 && git checkout 91d2d53f86c7b64a4f9aefd6183e1a5de4ea2970
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 0be247ce8b91ba3b9a3ce7235491b28a986b039a e029ea772b1555ea33b2946e0978ff4175dbdd3e && git checkout -B drift-repro 0be247ce8b91ba3b9a3ce7235491b28a986b039a && git merge --no-ff e029ea772b1555ea33b2946e0978ff4175dbdd3e

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 0be247ce8b91ba3b9a3ce7235491b28a986b039a
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 0be247ce8b91ba3b9a3ce7235491b28a986b039a` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `e029ea772b1555ea33b2946e0978ff4175dbdd3e`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/migrations/entries/semantic/18.formula-date-subtraction-refused.ts + packages/formula/src/cel-engine.ts, packages/formula/src/validate.ts, packages/formula/src/expression-refusal.ts, packages/formula/src/validate-date-text-arithmetic.test.ts, packages/formula/src/expression-refusal-codes.test.ts, packages/formula/src/validate.test.ts, packages/lint/src/validate-expressions.test.ts (the narrowing face's floor: every path of the diff outside the prose faces); read beside them, unchanged on this head: packages/formula/src/stdlib.ts, packages/formula/src/index.ts, packages/lint/src/validate-expressions.ts, packages/lint/src/authoring-rules.ts, packages/metadata-protocol/src/runtime-authoring-gate.ts, packages/objectql/src/engine.ts (`applyFormulaPlan`, `roundFormulaValue`), packages/spec/src/migrations/types.ts, packages/spec/src/migrations/entries/README.md. Prose faces (`.changeset/28944-formula-date-subtraction-refused.md`, `content/docs/data-modeling/formulas.mdx`) are the lane seat's ACCEPT at `TIER_DEFAULT`; the changeset's declaration lines are judged under ② below.

Reviewed against merge-base `135054ebaa7fb4f1282714d6856a0a6a032a81fe` (two commits on the head: `99ff16cdb`, `e029ea772`). Inputs: card #28944 with triage `6569503923`, the claim `6569744035` and the os-dev-report `6570740134`; #3306, #28660; the precedent changesets and D3 entries of #28596 and #28688; PR #29058's body, file list and net diff; the head's check-runs. The dispatch order was not an input to the judgments below.

### ① Derived judgments

1. **What the accept set loses, named.** At `validateExpression` (`packages/formula/src/validate.ts`, `typeSoundnessIssue` → new `dateTextIssue`), for a hint carrying `fieldTypes`, when `firstTypeMismatch` passes:
   - `date-text-arithmetic` (error, any role): an arithmetic operator (`+ - * / %`) on a `date`/`datetime` field's operand that the text typing cannot answer. Refused: `DateText - DateText` (date and datetime), `DateText ± Duration`, `Timestamp + DateText` / `DateText + Timestamp`, and the same inside a comparison (`record.end_date - record.start_date > duration("72h")`). **Right**: with the field typed as what `rewriteFaultedOperands` / `coercionFor` (`cel-engine.ts`) will see, the evaluator coerces a text operand only against a `number` or a `temporal` counterpart (a Date value, a `today()`/`now()`/`daysAgo`/`daysFromNow` call, a `date()`/`datetime()` call); a text counterpart (`valueKind` → `'string'`) and a `duration()` call (`operandKind` → `'unknown'`) get no coercion, so those pairs fault and the row reads null (`applyFormulaPlan`: `r.ok ? … : null`). The declared overload set in `registerDateTextOverloads` is exactly the complement: ordering and equality against another date field, text or a Timestamp (`bool`), `Timestamp - DateText` / `DateText - Timestamp` (`Duration`, the coerced case), `+` with text (concatenation), `== null`. Nothing is matched in the source text; the verdict is the checker's first fault, read through `UNSOUND_OVERLOAD_RE` and gated to an arithmetic operator with `DateText` on a side.
   - `date-duration-value` (error, `value` role only): a formula whose computed type is `google.protobuf.Duration`. Refused: `today() - record.start_date`, `now() - record.start_at`, `record.start_date - today()`, and any other Duration value (`today() - daysAgo(3)`). **Right, and within the ruling's spirit**: `applyFormulaPlan` writes `r.value` through `roundFormulaValue`, which passes a non-number through untouched, and no read door coerces a cel-js Duration object, so every Duration-valued formula serialises as `{}` (the dev's live REST reading `qa_since_today: {}` and `qa_dt_since_now: {}`, and the test's `JSON.stringify(r.value) === '{}'` pin, agree). A Duration is usable only when it is consumed inside the expression, and those shapes keep their value type and stay clean: `(today() - record.start_date).getHours()` (int) and a predicate comparing a duration (`today() - record.start_date > duration("72h")`, bool) are pinned clean. So the wider-than-two-shapes refusal does not over-reach: it refuses exactly the values that cannot reach a field, and nothing that can.
2. **Could the second pass refuse what the first accepts and the runtime answers? No.** `firstDateTextVerdict` returns a verdict on two paths only: (a) an arithmetic fault with `DateText` on a side, and (b) a clean check whose type is a Duration (and only in `value` role). Every other first fault (a function overload on the text, `in`, `size()`, `isoDate(record.d)`, an ordering against a number) returns `null` and is clean. Date comparisons (`<` against a date field, a literal, `today()` / `now()`), `==` / `!=` and the null guard, concatenation, `daysBetween(dyn, dyn)`, `addDays(dyn, dyn)` (stdlib declares them `dyn`), number subtraction and the flattened flow scope are all pinned clean, each row judged by `celEngine.evaluate` over a served row in the same test. The only cost is that a second typed parse now runs for every `value`-role expression and for every predicate on an object with a date field (`dateTextIssue` gates on that); masking stays conservative, as the PR says — a non-arithmetic first fault can hide a later date fault, never invent one.
3. **The `+ 1` shape keeps its words by ordering, not by special-casing.** `firstTypeMismatch` still answers first and is unchanged (its docblock gained a pointer only); `dateTextIssue` runs only when it returns `null`. The test pins `(record.end_date - record.start_date) + 1` → `date-arithmetic` with params `google.protobuf.Duration + int`, and the existing `date-arithmetic` pins in `expression-refusal-codes.test.ts` are untouched. **Right.**
4. **One judge for every face.** `os validate` / `os build` / `os lint` → `validateStackExpressions` → `validateExpression('value', …, { fieldTypes: fieldTypeIndex.get(objectName), scope: 'record', … })` for a formula field (`packages/lint/src/validate-expressions.ts`) and `validateExpression('predicate', …, { fieldTypes, scope, … })` for every object-bound predicate. The object save door → `runRuntimeAuthoringGate` → `runRuntimeAuthoringRules` → `AUTHORING_RULES` entry `validateStackExpressions` (`tier: 'gating'`, `commands: ALL`, `input: 'parsed'`, `packages/lint/src/authoring-rules.ts`), the same function over the written object plus the live universe. No lint source changed; the lint test pins the stack face (two errors, `daysBetween` clean). The dev's live readings (CLI exit 1 with four `expression-invalid` errors; save door 422 `INVALID_METADATA` for both shapes, 200 for `daysBetween`) are consistent with this wiring. **Right.**
5. **Datetime included after measurement.** The ruling made it conditional; the dev measured `record.end_at - record.start_at` → null (same `dyn‹string› - dyn‹string›` WARN) and `now() - record.start_at` → `{}` live, and the test table pins both rows against the evaluator. **Right.**
6. **Shipped formulas.** Read, not run: a `git grep` of `origin/main` (`packages/**`, `examples/**`, non-test, non-prose) and of the hotcrm checkout for a `today()`/`now()`/`*_date`/`*_at` operand on the left of a minus against a record field or temporal call finds no formula; hotcrm's one date span is `daysBetween(record.stage_entry_date, today())`. The dev's "no shipped formula is refused" holds. **Right.**
7. **Public surface moved.** On the `@objectstack/formula` entry (`packages/formula/src/index.ts`; `exports` is `.` only): `EXPRESSION_REFUSAL_CODES` (closed set) gains `date-text-arithmetic` and `date-duration-value`; the exported types `ExpressionRefusalCode` and `ExpressionRefusalParams` widen by those two members (additive). `firstDateTextVerdict` / `DateTextVerdict` are module exports of `cel-engine.ts` not re-exported from the entry, so they are not published. `check:api-surface` exit 0 (dev) and `Lint & Repo Gates` success on the head. The accept set of `validateExpression` narrows as in 1. **Right** — and this is why `Clause-②: yes` is the correct arm here where the two precedents (spec-only) carried `no`.
8. **ADR-0087 D3 entry** `packages/spec/src/migrations/entries/semantic/18.formula-date-subtraction-refused.ts`: `export const entry: SemanticMigration` with `id`, `surface`, `replacement`, `reason`, `acceptanceCriteria` (the five required fields of `SemanticMigration`, `types.ts`); the file name `18.<id>.ts` matches the `id`, which is what the generator concatenates into `MIGRATIONS_BY_MAJOR[18].semantic` (`entries/README.md`; `registry.ts` is generated and git-ignored, so no index edit is owed). The entry's shape matches the precedents `18.connector-instance-auth-inline-secret-refused` and `18.connector-entry-undeclared-key-refused`: a prose surface naming the doors, the replacement with the `daysBetween` forms, a reason that says why there is no mechanical rewrite, and acceptance criteria an upgrader can run. The `reason` also records that a stored formula of the refused shape held no usable value, so no stored data depends on it. **Well-formed and registered.** `check-adr-0087-registration.mjs --base origin/main` and `--self-test` exit 0 in the dev's gate record; `Check Changeset` and `Lint · PM dispatch-gates` are success on the head.
9. **No merge with `origin/main`, confirmed.** `origin/main` is 16 commits past `135054eb`; the set of files they touch (read with `git diff --name-only`) intersects the PR's file list nowhere, and the only `packages/spec/src` paths among them are `automation/*` and `shared/*`, outside `migrations/`. The 49 other open PRs (file lists read one by one) touch none of `packages/formula/src/**`, `packages/lint/src/validate-expressions*`, or the entry. **No overlap.**

### ② Semver level

- `.changeset/28944-formula-date-subtraction-refused.md`: `'@objectstack/formula': minor`, `'@objectstack/spec': minor`; line-initial `Clause-②: yes (narrowing)` and `Metadata-protocol: narrowed`; exactly one marker `<!-- adr-0087: registered formula-date-subtraction-refused -->`; a `**BREAKING**` banner; a `## FROM → TO` block with the one-line fix. The PR body carries the same two declaration lines. **Consistent** with AGENTS.md Post-Task Checklist 3: a value refused is `narrowed`; a kind takes at least `minor` on a package the diff moves (formula and spec both move; lint moves only a test and owes no changeset); `(narrowing)` is BREAKING and carries its migration and its ADR-0087 disposition. `minor` is what `check-changeset-no-major.mjs --base origin/main` admits (exit 0 in the gate record; `Check Changeset` success on the head).
- `Clause-②: yes` is the right arm (① 7): the published formula entry's accept set and code set moved. The precedents' `no (narrowing)` was for spec-only diffs and is not the model here.

### ③ Boundary flags

1. **`date-duration-value` is wider than the two named shapes** (dev flag, Acceptance notes). Answered in ① 1: every Duration-valued formula reads `{}` and nothing consumes a Duration from a field, so refusing the whole type is inside the order's "shapes that cannot produce a value"; the consuming shapes stay clean. Accepted.
2. **`Skills-docs: follow-up owed`** (PR body header line, and `out_of_scope_findings[0]` class b in the report). The line is not a recognised declaration: nothing under `scripts/pm/`, the pm-dispatch skill, `os-dev.md` or AGENTS.md reads a `Skills-docs:` key, so it is harmless to the body guards and binds nothing. The recognised carriers are the PR's `## Acceptance notes` and the report's `out_of_scope_findings` entry with `class:` + `reach:` + evidence + dedupe words (`os-dev.md` rule 3), which the report does carry; the PR body carries the finding as a header line instead of under `## Acceptance notes`. The substance is right: `skills/**` is a Tier H surface (AGENTS.md PD #14), outside this claim's file surface, and the callout at `skills/objectstack-formula/SKILL.md` lines 151–153 ("`end - start` does not fault — it yields a `duration` stored as `{}`") is now false twice over (it read null before this PR, and it is refused at build after it); `skills/objectstack-ui/evals/analytics-inline-vs-dataset.json` id 6 describes a stored `end_date - start_date` formula. **What the seat does**: file the class-b card in this repo with a `Seam:` line (the skill callout → `packages/formula/src/validate.ts` `dateTextIssue` / `cel-engine.ts` `firstDateTextVerdict`), then the ACCEPT lists the finding as `filed #N` and the carrier becomes that card (`carrier: #N`), replacing "follow-up owed"; the skill fix itself lands Tier H. No change to this PR is owed for it.
3. **`@objectstack/rest` bundles a copy of `@objectstack/formula` into `dist`** (`carrier: none · noted, not filed`). A built artifact, not source; it follows on rest's next build. Not a card under rule 3's three classes. Accepted as noted.
4. **Evidence arithmetic.** Red first on base: 10 red of 27 = the seven refused rows + the naming, flattened and role tests; the two `+ 1` rows and 13 controls green on base — consistent with the table. Ablation 1 (drop the text typing): 8 red = four `date-text-arithmetic` rows + naming + flattened + pin + sweep; ablation 2 (drop the duration-value arm): 7 red = three `date-duration-value` rows + naming + role + pin + sweep; each half reds only its own cases, so neither arm is carried by the other. 106/106 derived gates exit 0 (`28944-gates-ran.txt`); full dogfood 383 passed / 3 skipped (386), 3163 / 28 skipped (3191), VERDICT 0 at `e029ea77`. Consistent.
5. **CI on the head at review time.** 67 check-runs: every completed run is `success` or `skipped` (`Lint & Repo Gates`, `Governed Surface Queue Guard`, `Check Changeset` ×2, `Dogfood Regression Gate`, `Live E2E UI`, `Spec property liveness`, `PR-body guards`, all `Lint · *`, `Type Check · source gates` / `debt ledger`, `Build Docs`, `Build UI Deps`, `Check Documentation Links`); still `in_progress` at the last read: `Test Core` 1, 2, 5, 6 of 8 (3, 4, 7, 8 completed green), `Test UI` 4–10, 12–14, 16 of 16, `Type Check · workspace`, `Type Check UI`. No red at any read. The landing check ② (all checks green, read off the head) is the seat's before enqueue; this record's verdict is ①②③ and does not wait on it.
6. **Author.** PR `user.login` is `objectstack-fleet[bot]`; no author note owed.
7. **Residual, not a finding.** `offendingField` attributes `reference` to the first declared date field the source names, so a Duration formula that merely names a date field elsewhere (`record.start_date < today() ? duration("1h") : duration("2h")`) is worded "from `record.start_date`"; the same best-effort attribution `firstTypeMismatch` has always used. A predicate whose whole value is a Duration (`today() - record.d` as a condition) stays clean by design (pinned); its non-boolean type is another check's question.
